tldr: Page 70 of Appendix C: Survey Data contains individual responses from Oregon residents on prosperity drivers. Dominant themes: (1) Strong advocacy for universal Preschool for All, cited as delivering 3-to-1 return on investment and raising family incomes 22% on average; (2) High taxes and over-regulation blamed for business departures; (3) Permitting delays (40-day residential average), increased construction costs ($2,700-$3,000 per $450,000 home), and regulatory burdens; (4) Calls to preserve natural gas access; (5) Childcare affordability crisis (Oregon 49th of 50 states); (6) Workforce challenges and skills training needs.

bullets.text: Universal Preschool for All cited as delivering 3-to-1 return on investment and raising family incomes by 22% on average across multiple respondents
Oregon ranks 49th out of 50 states for childcare affordability according to Anders Liljeholm
Building permits increased 40% compared to 2024/2025 numbers, with residential permit lead time averaging 40 days, per Tristan Gillis
Regulatory requirements added average of $2,700-$3,000 in costs to $450,000 homes per Tristan Gillis (PARR)
Multiple respondents identify high taxes and over-regulation as primary drivers of business exodus from Oregon
Respondents advocate for preservation of natural gas availability and oppose restrictions on its use
Workforce challenges cited include difficulty finding reliable employees, childcare costs forcing departures, and need for skills training
ERIC BRANT GILL reports Oregon had 3rd highest unemployment rate in the country with businesses unable to remain viable
